Network Policy Server handles RADIUS authentication and policy. A VPN server connects remote devices to the network but runs nothing for them. A print server manages shared printers and queues.

prompt: Several internal applications must send email notifications, such as password-reset messages and job failure alerts, to users' mailboxes. Which type of server role should the administrator provide for these applications?

options.text: A directory server that stores email addresses for the applications
A messaging server or SMTP relay that accepts mail from the applications
A file server that holds a shared outbox folder for the applications
A DNS server that hosts MX records for each of the applications

explanation: Applications send email through a message server, typically an SMTP relay that accepts mail from approved hosts and delivers it. MX records tell senders where to deliver mail for a domain, but DNS does not send or relay messages. A directory server stores identities and addresses but does not transport mail. A shared outbox folder on a file server does not deliver messages to mailboxes.

prompt: A company is connecting its on-premises Active Directory to a cloud identity service. Security policy requires that user passwords are verified only by on-premises systems, and no password hashes may be stored in the cloud. Which hybrid identity approach meets this requirement?

options.text: Local accounts in the cloud service, created by hand with the same user names
Directory synchronization of user accounts only, with separate cloud-only passwords
Federation, which redirects sign-ins to an on-premises identity provider
Directory synchronization with password hash synchronization to the cloud directory

explanation: With federation, the cloud service trusts an on-premises identity provider, so passwords are checked on premises and no hashes need to be stored in the cloud. Password hash synchronization copies hashes of password hashes to the cloud directory, which the policy forbids. Syncing accounts with separate cloud-only passwords means passwords are verified in the cloud, not on premises. Hand-created cloud accounts are also verified in the cloud and add admin work.

prompt: A company is creating a virtual network in a public cloud and will connect it to the data center with a site-to-site VPN. The data center uses 10.0.0.0/16 and 10.1.0.0/16. Which address space should the administrator assign to the cloud virtual network?
explanation: Routing between connected networks only works when their address spaces do not overlap, and 10.50.0.0/16 does not overlap either on-premises range. 10.0.0.0/16 duplicates an existing on-premises network. 10.1.128.0/17 falls inside 10.1.0.0/16. 10.0.0.0/8 contains both on-premises ranges.

prompt: A company plans to move a reporting application to a public cloud. The application runs hundreds of queries per page load against a database that must stay on premises for compliance. Users complain that the cloud test environment is very slow. What is the best workload placement decision?

options.text: Keep the application in the cloud and add more memory to the on-premises database server
Keep the application in the cloud and switch the site-to-site VPN to a different VPN protocol
Keep the application on premises near the database, or move both together once compliance allows
Keep the application in the cloud and add more vCPUs to the cloud VM running the application

explanation: A chatty application that makes many round trips to its database is slowed by WAN latency, so it should be placed close to the data it uses. Extra vCPUs do not remove network round-trip delay. Adding database memory does not shorten the distance each query travels. Changing the VPN protocol does not remove the latency between the cloud region and the data center.

prompt: An administrator manages 60 Linux servers from a hardened jump host. Management sessions must be encrypted, and the security team wants password logins disabled for administrators. Which administrative interface and setting meet these requirements?

options.text: Telnet with key-based authentication, and password logins disabled in the telnet daemon
SSH with key-based authentication, and PasswordAuthentication set to no in sshd_config
RDP with Network Level Authentication, and the Remote Desktop Users group emptied
The local console through a KVM switch, with the root password removed from each server

explanation: SSH encrypts the session and supports public key authentication, and setting PasswordAuthentication no in sshd_config stops password logins. Telnet sends everything in clear text and has no key-based authentication. RDP is mainly a Windows protocol, and emptying the Remote Desktop Users group would just block access. A local KVM console does not provide remote encrypted access from the jump host, and removing root passwords weakens security.

prompt: A company is deploying Windows Server Core on all new file servers. Administrators want a browser-based graphical tool to manage the servers' storage, services and updates remotely. What should they use?

options.text: Remote Desktop with mstsc
An SSH session running vi
The local Server Manager console
Windows Admin Center

explanation: Windows Admin Center is a browser-based management tool that manages Server Core and other Windows servers remotely, including storage, services and updates. Remote Desktop to Server Core gives only a command prompt, not a graphical management tool. Server Manager cannot run locally on Server Core because it has no desktop shell. vi is a text editor and does not manage Windows services or storage.

prompt: An administrator needs to refresh the package list and install all available updates on an Ubuntu server. Which command does this?

options.text: sudo dnf check-update && sudo dnf upgrade
brew update && brew upgrade
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade
sudo yum makecache && sudo yum update

explanation: Ubuntu uses the apt package manager, where apt update refreshes the package index and apt upgrade installs available updates. dnf is the package manager for RHEL 8 and later, Fedora and related distributions, and yum is the older RHEL tool, so neither is used on Ubuntu. brew is the Homebrew package manager used mainly on macOS.

prompt: An administrator needs to install the DHCP Server role and its management tools on a Windows Server without using the GUI. Which PowerShell command should be used?

options.text: Add-DhcpServerv4Scope -Name DHCP -IncludeManagementTools
Install-WindowsFeature -Name DHCP -IncludeManagementTools
Start-Service -Name DHCPServer -IncludeManagementTools
Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName DHCP

explanation: Install-WindowsFeature installs server roles and features, and -IncludeManagementTools adds the related consoles and PowerShell modules. Add-DhcpServerv4Scope creates a scope on a DHCP server that already has the role installed, and it has no such parameter. Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature manages optional features on client and image editions rather than installing server roles with their tools. Start-Service starts an existing service and cannot install anything.

prompt: An administrator connects to a remote Linux server over SSH to run a database upgrade that will take about two hours. The administrator's VPN often drops for a few seconds, which ends the SSH session and kills any commands running in it. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Increase the terminal emulator's scrollback buffer so it keeps the output after a disconnect
Open a second SSH session as a backup so the upgrade keeps running if the first one drops
Start a terminal multiplexer such as tmux or screen on the server and run the upgrade inside it
Run the upgrade in a web-based terminal that reconnects automatically to the same SSH session

explanation: A terminal multiplexer keeps the shell session running on the server after the SSH connection drops, so the administrator can reattach and the upgrade continues. A second SSH session does not protect processes started in the first one. Scrollback only keeps output on the client and does nothing for the remote process. A browser-based terminal that opens a new SSH connection still loses the original session's processes when it drops.

prompt: A company has an aging physical server running a legacy application whose installer and vendor are no longer available. The hardware is out of warranty, and the company wants to keep the application running on its virtualization cluster. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Perform a virtual-to-virtual (V2V) conversion of the server into a VM on the cluster
Take a snapshot of the physical server and restore it as a container on the cluster
Rebuild the application on a new VM by installing it again from the vendor media
Perform a physical-to-virtual (P2V) conversion of the server into a VM on the cluster

explanation: A P2V conversion copies the running physical system, including the OS and installed application, into a VM, which avoids reinstalling software that can no longer be obtained. V2V converts an existing VM between platforms, and this server is physical. Physical servers do not have hypervisor snapshots, and a full OS image cannot simply become a container. Reinstalling is not possible because the installer is no longer available.

prompt: A company is moving 200 VMs from one hypervisor platform to a different vendor's hypervisor. Each VM's virtual disks and hardware settings must be changed to the format the new platform uses. Which migration strategy is this?

options.text: Virtual-to-virtual (V2V) migration
Physical-to-virtual (P2V) migration
Live migration within a cluster
Storage migration within a datastore

explanation: V2V migration converts VMs from one virtualization platform to another, including converting disk formats such as VMDK to VHDX and adjusting virtual hardware. P2V applies to physical servers, not existing VMs. Live migration moves a running VM between hosts of the same platform without conversion. Storage migration moves a VM's files between storage locations on the same platform.

prompt: An administrator builds a test VM on a hypervisor host. The VM needs to download updates from the internet, but systems on the corporate LAN must not be able to initiate connections to it. Which virtual networking mode should the administrator use?

options.text: NAT, so the VM shares the host's address for outbound traffic
Bridged, so the VM gets its own address on the corporate LAN
Private, so the VM can talk only to other VMs on the same host
Host-only, so the VM can talk only to the host and its other VMs

explanation: In NAT mode, the VM's traffic is translated to the host's address, so the VM can reach the internet while LAN systems cannot reach it unless port forwarding is configured. Bridged mode puts the VM directly on the LAN with its own address, so LAN systems can reach it. Private and host-only networks keep the VM off external networks entirely, so it could not download updates.

prompt: A new VM will run a departmental web application that users on the LAN reach by its own IP address, just like a physical server. Which virtual networking mode should the VM's network adapter use?

options.text: Internal, connected only to the host and VMs on the same host
Bridged, through an external switch to the physical network
NAT, translated through the hypervisor host's own network address
Private, connected only to the other VMs on the same host

explanation: Bridged networking, such as a Hyper-V external switch, connects the VM to the physical network so it gets its own LAN address that users can reach directly. With NAT, the VM hides behind the host's address and is not directly reachable without port forwarding. Internal and private switches do not connect to the physical network at all, so LAN users could not reach the VM.

prompt: An administrator is building an isolated malware analysis lab on a Hyper-V host. The lab VMs must communicate with each other, but not with the host or any physical network. Which type of virtual switch should be used?

options.text: Internal virtual switch
External virtual switch
Private virtual switch
External switch with host sharing disabled

explanation: A Hyper-V private virtual switch allows traffic only among VMs connected to it, with no connection to the host or physical network. An internal switch also connects the host's management OS to the VMs. An external switch connects to a physical NIC, and disabling host sharing only removes the host's access while the VMs still reach the physical network.

prompt: A Linux VM's network throughput is far lower than other VMs on the same host. Its virtual NIC is an emulated legacy adapter type, while the other VMs use the hypervisor's paravirtualized adapter with guest drivers installed. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Add a second emulated adapter to the VM and team the two adapters inside the guest
Increase the VM's vCPU count so it can process more packets through the emulated adapter
Replace the emulated adapter with a paravirtualized vNIC, such as VMXNET3 or virtio-net
Move the VM to a private virtual switch so its traffic avoids the host's physical NICs

explanation: Paravirtualized vNICs work with guest drivers that know they run in a VM, which avoids the overhead of emulating real hardware and gives much higher throughput. Teaming two emulated adapters still carries the emulation overhead. A private switch would cut the VM off from the physical network. More vCPUs may help a little but do not remove the emulation bottleneck.

prompt: A VM running a low-latency trading application needs near line-rate network performance, and the administrator wants its traffic to bypass the hypervisor's software virtual switch. The host NIC supports SR-IOV. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Enable jumbo frames on the VM's emulated adapter so it sends fewer, larger packets
Enable NAT on the virtual switch so the VM's traffic uses the host's network stack
Enable a second virtual switch and connect the VM to both switches for more bandwidth
Enable SR-IOV and assign a virtual function of the physical NIC directly to the VM

explanation: SR-IOV splits a physical NIC into virtual functions that can be given directly to VMs, so traffic bypasses the software virtual switch and latency drops. NAT adds translation through the host stack and increases latency. Jumbo frames may reduce packet count but the emulated adapter and virtual switch remain in the path. A second virtual switch still processes the traffic in software.

prompt: A developer runs a database inside a container and stores its data in the container's writable layer. After the container is removed and a new one is started from the same image, the database is empty. How should the administrator prevent this?

options.text: Commit the running container to a new image every night as a backup
Store the database files on a persistent volume mounted into the container
Increase the container's memory limit so its data is kept in memory longer
Restart the container instead of removing it whenever the image changes

explanation: A container's writable layer is deleted when the container is removed, so persistent data belongs on a volume that lives outside the container lifecycle. Committing running containers to images mixes data into images and is not a proper data strategy. Avoiding container removal is not sustainable because updates replace containers. Memory limits do not make data persist after the container is removed.

prompt: A security scan finds a vulnerable library in a containerised web service running in production. What is the recommended way to apply the fix?

options.text: Pause the running containers, copy the patched library into them, and then resume the containers
Add a firewall rule that blocks the library's port, leaving the existing images and containers as they are
Open a shell in each running container and upgrade the library with the package manager in place
Rebuild the image with the patched library and redeploy containers from it

explanation: Containers are meant to be immutable, so the fix goes into a rebuilt image and new containers replace the old ones, which keeps every instance consistent and reproducible. Patching inside running containers is lost when they are replaced and causes drift. Copying files into paused containers has the same problem. A firewall rule does not fix a vulnerable library and often cannot block a flaw that is reached through the application itself.

prompt: A VM was given 16 vCPUs when it was deployed. Monitoring shows the guest averages 8 percent CPU use, and the host reports high CPU ready time for this VM and others on the host. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Add more vCPUs to the VM so its work finishes sooner and frees the host
Move the VM to a host with more cores while keeping the same vCPU count
Set a CPU reservation equal to all 16 vCPUs so the VM is always scheduled
Rightsize the VM by reducing its vCPU count to match its actual demand

explanation: An oversized VM makes the scheduler find many free physical cores at once, which raises ready time; reducing vCPUs to match actual use improves scheduling for it and its neighbours. Adding vCPUs makes the problem worse. Reserving all 16 vCPUs locks host capacity the VM does not use. Moving it keeps the waste and spreads the problem to another host.

prompt: A datastore of 10 TB holds thin-provisioned virtual disks with a total provisioned size of 18 TB, of which 7 TB is actually written. What risk must the administrator manage?

options.text: The virtual disks will be converted to thick disks once the 10 TB is exceeded
The VMs will see only 10 TB in total and report their disks as smaller than provisioned
The hypervisor will reject new writes until the provisioned size is reduced to 10 TB
If the VMs keep writing, the datastore can fill up and VMs on it can pause or fail

explanation: Thin provisioning overcommits storage, so if the written data grows past the datastore's real capacity, writes fail and VMs can stop, which is why use must be monitored with alerts and headroom. Thin disks are not converted to thick automatically. The hypervisor does not limit writes based on provisioned size while space remains. Each VM sees its full provisioned disk size, regardless of the datastore's actual capacity.

prompt: A virtualization cluster has hosts with two different processor generations from the same CPU vendor. Live migrations of running VMs fail between the newer and older hosts because of CPU feature differences. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A CPU compatibility mode that presents a common baseline of CPU features to the VMs
A higher memory reservation on each VM so the migration copies memory faster
A dedicated migration network with jumbo frames between every pair of hosts
A larger number of vCPUs on each VM so that both CPU generations are used

explanation: Hypervisors offer CPU compatibility features, such as VMware EVC or Hyper-V processor compatibility mode, that hide newer CPU features so VMs can move between hosts of different generations. Memory reservations do not affect CPU feature checks. A faster migration network helps transfer speed but does not resolve feature mismatches. Adding vCPUs has no effect on which CPU instructions the VM sees.

prompt: A critical VM must always have at least 32 GB of physical memory available, even when the host is under memory pressure from other VMs. Which resource setting should the administrator configure?

options.text: Memory ballooning enabled on the VM
A memory limit of 32 GB on the VM
A memory reservation of 32 GB on the VM
Higher memory shares on the VM

explanation: A reservation guarantees that the specified amount of physical memory is available to the VM. A limit sets a maximum, not a minimum, so it would not protect the VM. Shares only give the VM priority relative to others during contention and guarantee nothing. Ballooning lets the hypervisor reclaim memory from the guest, which is the opposite of what is needed.

prompt: An administrator uses PowerShell Desired State Configuration to define that a set of Windows servers must have IIS installed and a specific service running. Someone later stops the service on one server. With the Local Configuration Manager set to ApplyAndAutoCorrect, what happens?

options.text: The server logs the drift but leaves the service stopped until an administrator approves it
The server reinstalls IIS from scratch to return to the state in its original configuration
The server stops applying the configuration because a manual change overrides DSC settings
On its next consistency check, the server detects the drift and starts the service again

explanation: With ApplyAndAutoCorrect, the Local Configuration Manager periodically checks the node against its configuration and corrects any drift, so the service is started again. ApplyAndMonitor is the mode that only reports drift. DSC fixes only the resources that are out of compliance rather than reinstalling everything. Manual changes do not stop DSC from enforcing the configuration.

prompt: A VM is given a physical GPU through device passthrough so a machine learning workload can use it directly. What is a common trade-off of this configuration?

options.text: The VM must run a Type 2 hypervisor inside it, because passthrough needs a nested hypervisor
The VM is tied to the host with the GPU, which typically prevents live migration to other hosts
The VM can only use half of the GPU's memory, because the host keeps the rest for itself
The VM loses its virtual NIC, because passthrough devices replace all emulated hardware

explanation: With passthrough the VM controls the physical device directly, so it depends on that host's hardware and usually cannot be live-migrated. The VM gets the whole device, not a fixed share kept by the host. Passthrough needs IOMMU support on the host, not a nested hypervisor in the guest. Other virtual devices such as the vNIC remain in place.

prompt: A VDI host runs many desktop VMs that are idle much of the day. The administrator wants to fit more VMs per host by letting each VM's memory grow and shrink with demand. A separate SQL Server VM on another host must have predictable memory performance. Which memory configuration is most appropriate?

options.text: Use dynamic memory for all of the VMs so each host can reclaim unused memory
Use static memory for the desktop VMs and dynamic memory for the SQL Server VM
Use static memory for all of the VMs and add memory to the hosts to raise density
Use dynamic memory for the desktop VMs and static memory for the SQL Server VM

explanation: Dynamic memory suits many lightly used VMs because the host can reclaim memory from idle guests and run more of them, while a database server benefits from a fixed allocation that the host never takes away. Reversing the assignment removes the density gain and gives the database unpredictable memory. Dynamic memory for the database risks reclaiming memory it uses for caching. Static memory everywhere gives up the density goal.

prompt: A two-node active-active cluster serves a web application. During normal operation, each node runs at about 70 percent CPU. What is the main risk with this design?

options.text: If one node fails, the survivor needs about 140 percent of its capacity
Clients receive duplicate replies from both nodes
If both nodes stay online, the heartbeat traffic uses the remaining 30 percent of each node's CPU
If one node fails, the cluster must wait for an administrator to start the standby node by hand

explanation: In an active-active design, each node must have enough headroom to absorb the other's load, and two nodes at 70 percent would need 140 percent of a single node after a failure. There is no idle standby in active-active; both nodes already serve traffic. Heartbeat traffic is tiny and does not consume large amounts of CPU. A load balancer sends each request to one node, so clients do not get duplicate replies.

prompt: In a two-node failover cluster, the dedicated heartbeat link between the nodes failed. Both nodes stayed up, each concluded the other had failed and tried to bring the same clustered disk and IP address online. Which configuration would prevent this?

options.text: A round-robin DNS record for the cluster name, so clients alternate between the two nodes
A shorter heartbeat interval on the existing link, so failures are detected more quickly
A quorum witness, so only the partition holding a majority of votes stays online
A second application instance on each node, so both nodes serve clients when the heartbeat stops

explanation: This is split-brain, and a quorum witness gives a tie-breaking vote so that only one partition keeps quorum and owns the resources; a second heartbeat path also helps. Running two active copies of a resource that must have one owner makes the conflict worse. A shorter interval detects the failure faster but still leaves both nodes believing they should take over. Round-robin DNS spreads clients but does nothing to stop both nodes claiming the same disk.

prompt: A load balancer sends incoming connections to three web servers in turn: first, second, third, then back to the first, regardless of how busy each server is. Two of the servers are new and have twice the capacity of the old one, and the old server is overloaded. Which change best addresses this?

options.text: Keep round-robin and lower the health check interval so the old server is marked down faster
Keep round-robin and enable session persistence so clients stay on the server they first used
Switch from plain round-robin to a weighted method that sends more connections to the larger servers
Keep round-robin and add a second load balancer in front of the existing one for redundancy

explanation: Plain round-robin hands out connections equally in sequence, so servers of unequal capacity get equal shares; a weighted method sends more work to the larger servers. A second load balancer adds redundancy but keeps the same distribution. Session persistence keeps clients on one server and can make imbalance worse. A faster health check might eject the old server only after it is already failing, rather than balancing load correctly.

prompt: A host connects to a storage array over two paths and uses the Most Recently Used (MRU) path selection policy. The primary path failed and I/O moved to the second path. After the primary path is repaired, I/O continues on the second path. Why?

options.text: MRU marks a path as permanently dead after a failure until the host is rebooted and rescans storage
MRU sends I/O across all paths in turn, and the repaired path is waiting for its turn in the rotation
MRU always prefers the path with the highest number, and the second path has the higher number
MRU keeps using the path that is currently working and does not fail back when the original path returns

explanation: The Most Recently Used policy stays on the path it is currently using and only switches when that path fails, so it does not return to the original path automatically. Rotating I/O across paths describes round-robin. MRU does not mark recovered paths dead until a reboot. A fixed policy with a preferred path, not MRU, is what returns to a chosen path when it comes back.

prompt: A company is choosing between a dedicated hardware load-balancing appliance and a software load balancer running on VMs for a new application platform. The platform's traffic changes a lot from month to month, and the team wants to add capacity quickly through automation. Which statement best supports choosing the software load balancer?

options.text: Software load balancers always deliver higher throughput than hardware appliances that use dedicated chips
Software load balancers need no health checks of back-end servers
Software load balancers can be deployed and scaled out through automation with no new hardware
Software load balancers remove the load balancer as a single point of failure without any extra instances

explanation: A software load balancer runs on general-purpose compute, so new instances can be added through automation as demand changes, without procurement. Hardware appliances with dedicated chips often have higher raw throughput, so software is not always faster. Software load balancers still need health checks to detect failed back-end servers. One software instance is still a single point of failure unless redundant instances are deployed.

prompt: An administrator creates a NIC team on a server using LACP (dynamic link aggregation) across two ports. The team shows both members as disconnected from the team, although both links are physically up. The switch ports are configured as ordinary trunk ports. What should be done?

options.text: Configure the two switch ports as members of an LACP port channel that matches the server's team
Configure spanning tree to block one switch port so the team uses only a single active link
Configure the server team in active-passive mode so that LACP is negotiated by the standby member
Configure each switch port in a different VLAN so the two team members do not create a loop

explanation: LACP is negotiated between the server and the switch, so the switch ports must be configured as an LACP port channel (link aggregation group) for the team members to join. Active-passive teaming is a different mode that does not negotiate LACP. Putting the ports in different VLANs breaks the aggregation. Blocking a port with spanning tree defeats the purpose of the team.

prompt: A company runs its primary application in its own data center and replicates the VMs to a public cloud provider. If the data center becomes unavailable, the VMs are started in the cloud and users connect there. Which redundancy approach does this describe?

options.text: Hybrid failover between on-premises infrastructure and a cloud environment
NIC teaming between two adapters inside each of the application servers
A hot spare drive in the storage array that rebuilds the RAID set automatically
Active-active clustering between two nodes in the same data center rack

explanation: Hybrid failover uses a cloud environment as the recovery target for on-premises workloads, so service continues there when the data center is lost. NIC teaming protects against a failed adapter or link within one server. A cluster in a single rack does not survive the loss of the data center. A hot spare protects against a failed drive inside one array.

prompt: A company plans a cluster stretched across two data centers 300 km apart, with storage replicated synchronously so that no committed write is lost if one site fails. Testing shows that application write latency becomes unacceptable. What is the cause?

options.text: Synchronous replication writes each block to tape at the remote site
Each write waits for the remote site to confirm it, so the round trip adds latency to every write
Synchronous replication compresses every write before sending it, so CPU use on the storage array slows the writes
Synchronous replication sends writes only when the link is idle, so busy periods queue the writes at the source site

explanation: With synchronous replication a write is not acknowledged until both sites have stored it, so the round trip over a long distance is added to every write. Waiting for idle link time describes asynchronous or background replication, which does not add this per-write delay. Compression is not what makes synchronous replication slow here. Replication writes go to the remote storage system, not tape.

prompt: A RAID 5 array of six drives on a server includes a seventh drive configured as a hot spare. One of the array members fails at 2:00 AM. What happens next?

options.text: The controller automatically rebuilds the array onto the hot spare
The controller waits until a technician removes the failed drive before it uses the hot spare
The controller converts the array to RAID 6 using the spare
The controller copies the hot spare onto the failed drive once the failed drive is replaced

explanation: A hot spare is an idle drive that the controller uses automatically to rebuild a degraded array, which shortens the time the array runs without redundancy. The rebuild does not need the failed drive removed first. A hot spare is not used to change the RAID level. The failed drive is replaced later, and the replacement may become the new spare or be copied back depending on the controller.

prompt: A server has six 4 TB drives. The array must survive the failure of any two drives at the same time while giving as much usable capacity as possible. Which RAID level should the administrator choose, and how much usable capacity results?

options.text: RAID 0, with about 24 TB usable
RAID 10, with about 12 TB usable
RAID 6, with about 16 TB usable
RAID 5, with about 20 TB usable

explanation: RAID 6 uses two drives' worth of parity, so it survives any two drive failures and gives (6 - 2) x 4 TB = 16 TB. RAID 10 gives 12 TB and survives two failures only if they are in different mirrors, not any two drives. RAID 5 gives 20 TB but survives only one drive failure. RAID 0 uses all 24 TB but has no redundancy, so a single drive failure destroys the array.

prompt: A database server performs a very high rate of small random writes. The administrator is choosing between RAID 5 and RAID 10 using the same drives. Why is RAID 10 usually the better choice?

options.text: RAID 10 mirrors each write with no parity math, avoiding RAID 5's read-modify-write penalty
RAID 10 stores data without redundancy, so it does no extra work and also tolerates a single drive failure
RAID 10 stripes parity across every drive, so it needs fewer drives than RAID 5 for the same usable capacity
RAID 10 keeps a single parity drive that every small write updates

explanation: In RAID 10 each write goes to both drives of a mirror, while a small write in RAID 5 needs the old data and parity to be read and new data and parity written, which costs about four I/Os per write. RAID 10 has no parity and needs more drives than RAID 5 for the same usable capacity. A single dedicated parity drive describes RAID 4, not RAID 10. RAID 10 does provide redundancy; RAID 0 is the level with none.

prompt: An administrator is choosing between a hardware RAID controller with a battery-protected write cache and software RAID provided by the operating system for a busy server's data volumes. Which statement is accurate?

options.text: Hardware RAID needs the OS to rebuild failed drives after each boot
Software RAID always keeps a battery-backed cache in host memory that survives a power failure
Software RAID uses a dedicated processor on the drives, so it puts no extra load on the host CPU
Hardware RAID offloads parity work, and a protected write cache speeds writes safely

explanation: A hardware RAID controller has its own processor for parity and rebuilds, and a battery- or flash-protected cache lets it acknowledge writes quickly without losing them in a power failure. Software RAID, such as Linux mdadm or Windows Storage Spaces, uses the host CPU. Hardware controllers rebuild on their own without the OS. Host memory used by software RAID is not battery-backed and is lost when power fails.

prompt: One of the two power supplies in a production server has failed. The server documentation lists the power supplies as hot-swappable. What can the administrator do?

options.text: Move the server's power cord to the working supply, because the failed one must stay installed
Replace the failed power supply while the server keeps running on the remaining supply
Disable the failed supply in firmware, because hot-swap parts can only be changed at boot time
Schedule downtime, because the server must be shut down before removing any power supply

explanation: Hot-swappable components can be removed and replaced while the system is running, so with a redundant supply the server stays online during the swap. A shutdown is not needed for hot-swap parts. The failed supply can be removed rather than left in place. Hot-swap means replacement during operation, not at boot time.

prompt: An e-commerce site runs on four identical web VMs behind a load balancer. During a sale, the platform automatically adds six more identical VMs, and after the sale it removes them. Which elasticity actions does this describe?

options.text: Vertical scaling: scaling up during the sale and scaling down afterwards
Horizontal scaling: scaling in during the sale and scaling out afterwards
Horizontal scaling: scaling out during the sale and scaling in afterwards
Vertical scaling: scaling out during the sale and scaling in afterwards

explanation: Adding more instances of the same size is horizontal scaling, called scaling out, and removing them is scaling in. Vertical scaling (scaling up or down) changes the size of existing VMs, such as adding vCPUs or memory. Scaling in removes capacity, so it cannot describe adding VMs for the sale. Scaling out and in are horizontal actions, not vertical ones.

prompt: A Linux administrator needs a backup script at /opt/scripts/backup.sh to run at 2:30 AM every Sunday. Which crontab entry should the administrator add?

options.text: 30 2 * 0 * /opt/scripts/backup.sh
30 2 * * 0 /opt/scripts/backup.sh
30 2 0 * * /opt/scripts/backup.sh
2 30 * * 0 /opt/scripts/backup.sh

explanation: Crontab fields are minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week, so '30 2 * * 0' runs at 02:30 every Sunday (day of week 0). '2 30 * * 0' swaps minute and hour and 30 is not a valid hour. '30 2 0 * *' and '30 2 * 0 *' put 0 in the day-of-month and month fields, which only accept values starting at 1.

prompt: A Windows Server administrator has a PowerShell maintenance script that must run every time the server boots, even when no one signs in. Which approach meets the requirement?

options.text: Add the script to the logon script field of the administrator's user account in the directory service
A Task Scheduler task with an At startup trigger, set to run whether or not a user is logged on
Place a shortcut to the script in the Startup folder of the administrator's user profile
Add a crontab entry with the @reboot keyword that calls powershell.exe with the script path

explanation: A Task Scheduler task with an At startup trigger, configured to run whether the user is logged on or not, runs at boot without an interactive session. The Startup folder and a logon script only run when that user signs in. cron and the @reboot keyword are Unix scheduling features that Windows Server does not provide.

prompt: A custom monitoring agent written in Python must start automatically when a Linux server boots and must be restarted automatically if it crashes. What is the best way to run it?

options.text: As a one-time job submitted with the at command that is scheduled for the next boot time
As a command appended to the administrator's ~/.bashrc file so it starts with each shell
As a cron job with the @reboot keyword that launches the script in the background
As a systemd service unit with Restart=on-failure, enabled with systemctl enable

explanation: Running the agent as a daemon under systemd with Restart=on-failure starts it at boot once enabled and restarts it when it exits with an error. A cron @reboot job starts it once at boot but nothing restarts it after a crash. ~/.bashrc runs only when that user opens an interactive shell, and an at job runs once at a fixed time.

prompt: A team must push configuration changes to 300 Linux servers. Security policy forbids installing management agents on the servers, but the team already has SSH key access to all of them. Which orchestration tool fits best?

options.text: Chef
Ansible
Task Scheduler
Puppet

explanation: Ansible is agentless: it connects to managed nodes over SSH and runs tasks defined in YAML playbooks. Puppet and Chef normally rely on an agent installed on each managed node that checks in with a central server. Task Scheduler is a Windows job scheduler, not a tool for orchestrating hundreds of Linux servers.

prompt: An organization wants every server to check in with a central server on a schedule, receive a compiled catalog built from declarative manifests, and automatically correct any configuration drift it finds. Which tool is designed around this model?

options.text: Puppet
cron
Ansible
Bash

explanation: Puppet agents periodically pull a catalog compiled from declarative manifests on the Puppet server and enforce the desired state, which corrects drift. Ansible pushes changes from a control node over SSH and does not use agents or catalogs by default. cron only schedules commands, and Bash is a shell language with no built-in desired-state enforcement.

prompt: An administrator must write one automation script that runs unchanged on both Windows Server and Linux hosts and works with structured objects rather than plain text in the pipeline. Which language is the best choice?

options.text: Korn shell (ksh)
PowerShell 7
Visual Basic Script (VBS)
Batch

explanation: PowerShell 7 runs on Windows, Linux and macOS, and its pipeline passes .NET objects between commands. Batch files and VBS run only on Windows, and Microsoft has deprecated VBScript. ksh is a Unix shell that works with text streams and is not native to Windows Server.

prompt: A PowerShell script wraps a Copy-Item command in a try/catch block, but when the destination share is unreachable the error is printed and the script carries on without entering the catch block. What change makes the catch block run?

options.text: Run Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass before the script runs
Move the Copy-Item command into a separate function
Add -ErrorAction Stop to the Copy-Item command
Replace the try/catch block with Write-Host statements

explanation: Copy-Item raises a non-terminating error by default, and try/catch only catches terminating errors, so -ErrorAction Stop turns the failure into one the catch block handles. The execution policy controls whether scripts may run at all, not how errors are handled. Moving the command into a function or adding Write-Host output does not change the error type.

prompt: Before scheduling a new Bash deployment script, an administrator wants to check it for syntax errors without running any of its commands. Which command should the administrator use?

options.text: bash -v deploy.sh
chmod +x deploy.sh
bash -x deploy.sh
bash -n deploy.sh

explanation: The -n option makes Bash read the commands and report syntax errors without executing them. -x and -v both run the script, printing each command as it is traced or read. chmod +x only marks the file as executable and does not check its contents.

prompt: A junior administrator has written a script that rewrites firewall rules on all web servers. The script has never been run before. What should happen before it is run against production?

options.text: Run it on all production servers at once but with verbose logging turned on for the first run
Add a comment block at the top that lists the firewall rules the script is expected to change
Run it first in a sandbox of non-production servers that copy the production firewall setup
Run it on a single production web server during business hours and watch for user complaints

explanation: A sandbox that copies the production setup lets the team see what the script really does without risking an outage. Running it on a production server, even one, still exposes users to a failure, and verbose logging only records a failure after it happens. Comments are good documentation but do not prove the script works.

prompt: A team's scripts are kept on a file share as copies named like cleanup_v2_final.ps1 and cleanup_v3_jsmith.ps1. The team needs to see who changed each line, compare versions and roll back to any earlier release. What should the team adopt?

options.text: A change log comment block at the top of each script that every editor must update
A naming rule that adds the date and the editor's initials to every saved copy of a script
A nightly backup of the file share so that any older copy of a script can be restored
A Git repository with commits for each change and tags for released versions

explanation: Version control such as Git records every change with its author, shows differences between versions and lets the team check out or revert to any tagged release. Nightly backups restore whole files but do not show line-level history or authorship. Comment blocks and naming rules depend on people remembering to update them and still give no reliable diff or rollback.

prompt: An edited cleanup script went into production and deleted the wrong directory because a path variable was mistyped. The manager wants a second administrator to check every script change before it can be merged and deployed. Which best practice does this describe?

options.text: Code documentation
Code review
Code syntax checking
Error handling

explanation: Code review has a second person examine changes before they are merged, which is how a mistyped path is most likely to be caught. Error handling deals with failures while a script runs, but a valid but wrong path does not raise an error. Documentation explains the code, and a syntax check would accept a variable that is spelled correctly but holds the wrong path.

prompt: New team members keep calling the author of a PowerShell provisioning script because they cannot tell what its parameters do or what output to expect. What should the author add so the information is available from Get-Help?

options.text: A comment-based help block with .SYNOPSIS, .PARAMETER and .EXAMPLE sections
A digital signature from the internal code-signing certificate authority
Shorter variable and function names so the script is quicker for new readers to scan
A Set-StrictMode -Version Latest line at the top of the script file

explanation: Comment-based help keywords such as .SYNOPSIS, .PARAMETER and .EXAMPLE document the script in a way that Get-Help can display. Shorter variable names make code harder, not easier, to understand. Set-StrictMode catches some coding mistakes, and a signature proves who published the script, but neither explains how to use it.

prompt: An administrator wants help from an AI assistant to diagnose repeated service crashes. The logs contain internal hostnames, IP addresses and customer account numbers, and policy classifies them as confidential. Only a public consumer chatbot is available. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Paste the full logs into the public chatbot, because the vendor deletes conversations after a period
Send the full logs to the chatbot in several small pieces so that no single prompt holds much data
Redact the confidential values first, or analyze the logs with an approved internal AI tool
Sign in to the public chatbot with a personal account so the logs are not linked to the company

explanation: Confidential data must not go to an external AI service that is not approved for it, so the logs need to be sanitized first or analyzed with an approved internal tool. A vendor's retention period does not make the disclosure acceptable. A personal account and splitting the data into pieces still send confidential data outside the organization.

prompt: An AI assistant produced a PowerShell script that disables user accounts listed in a CSV file. The administrator has to process 2,000 accounts tonight. What should the administrator do before running the script against the directory?

options.text: Run the script against all accounts with a Domain Admins account so it cannot fail for lack of rights
Run the script during the change window as written, because AI-generated code is checked by the vendor before it is shown
Ask the AI assistant to confirm that its script is correct and then run it against all 2,000 accounts
Review every command, verify unfamiliar cmdlets against vendor documentation, and test on a few test accounts

explanation: AI-generated code can contain invented parameters or logic errors, so a person must review it, check it against documentation and test it on a small scope before production use. Asking the same model to grade its own output is not independent verification. Extra privileges only increase the damage a faulty script can do, and AI output is not guaranteed to be tested.

prompt: A storage team exports 18 months of daily volume usage figures and asks an AI tool to estimate when each array will reach 90% capacity so purchases can be planned. Which AI use case is this?

options.text: Scripts and templates (code assistance)
Issue diagnosis
Professional development
Forecasting and predicting

explanation: Projecting future capacity from historical trends is forecasting and predicting. Issue diagnosis looks for the cause of a current problem, code assistance helps write scripts, and professional development is about building the administrator's own skills.

prompt: A company is connecting an AI operations assistant to its hypervisor management API so the assistant can restart virtual machines that stop responding. Which configuration best follows security best practice?

options.text: An API key shared by the whole operations team, so the assistant uses the same access as the team
The senior administrator's own account, so its actions match what an experienced engineer would do
A dedicated service account limited to the VM power actions it needs, with every action logged
A built-in full administrator account, so the assistant never fails on missing permissions

explanation: Giving the integration its own least-privilege account limits what it can do if it misbehaves or is compromised, and logging makes its actions auditable. Using a person's account or a shared team key blurs accountability and grants far more access than needed. A full administrator account breaks least privilege.

prompt: An administrator applied a tuning change suggested by an AI assistant without testing it, and the database cluster went down for two hours. Management asks who is accountable for the outage. Which statement reflects responsible AI use?

options.text: The cluster vendor is accountable, because its product should have rejected a harmful tuning change
No one is accountable, because the recommendation came from an automated system rather than a person
The AI vendor is accountable, because its assistant produced the faulty recommendation that was applied
The administrator and the organization, because people must validate AI output before acting on it

explanation: Liability for changes stays with the people and organization that decide to apply them, so AI suggestions must be reviewed and tested like any other change. AI vendors' terms generally do not make them responsible for how customers use output. Calling the system automated does not remove accountability, and the database vendor did not make the change.

prompt: After an outage, an administrator asks an AI assistant to draft a status update for customers. The draft states a root cause that the team has not confirmed yet. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Ask the AI to make the wording sound more confident so customers are reassured about the cause
Remove the unconfirmed cause and send the update through the normal approval process
Send the draft as written, because the AI assistant had access to the incident ticket when writing it
Send the draft without the company's name so that the unconfirmed root cause cannot be traced

explanation: AI can help draft communication, but a person must check it for accuracy and send it through the approved process, so unconfirmed causes must be removed. Having the ticket does not mean the AI's conclusion is right. Removing the company name or making false claims sound more certain is misleading and unethical.

prompt: While researching a fix, an AI assistant tells an administrator to use a command-line switch that the administrator has never seen. What is the best next step?

options.text: Use the switch only if the assistant also provides a link, because a link proves the switch exists
Ask the assistant to repeat its answer several times and use the switch if the answers match
Run the command on a production server straight away, because AI research tools draw on vendor documentation
Check the vendor documentation or man page to confirm the switch exists and works as described

explanation: AI tools can invent options that look plausible, so the switch must be checked against the authoritative documentation first. AI output does not always match vendor documentation. Repeating the same answer is not independent confirmation, and links supplied by an AI can also be wrong or unrelated.

prompt: Policy says confidential data must never be sent to external AI services, yet a review shows staff pasting server configuration files into unapproved AI websites. How can the organization enforce the policy technically?

options.text: Run a training session each quarter that explains which data classifications exist
Ask every employee to sign an annual acknowledgment that they have read the AI usage policy
Add a reminder about the AI usage policy to the sign-in banner shown on every server
Use DLP and web filtering rules that block confidential content and unapproved AI sites

explanation: Data loss prevention and web filtering enforce the policy technically by detecting or blocking classified content and unapproved destinations. Signed acknowledgments, banners and training are administrative controls that raise awareness but cannot stop someone from pasting data into a website.

prompt: A healthcare provider wants AI help analyzing server and application logs that may contain patient information. Regulations prohibit sending the data to third parties without an agreement, and none exists with any AI vendor. Which option fits best?

options.text: An AI model hosted internally on the provider's own infrastructure
A free public AI chatbot, used only from a computer that is not joined to the provider's domain
An external AI service, used after removing the server names but leaving the patient fields
An external AI service, used only by administrators who are cleared to see patient records

explanation: An internally hosted model keeps the data inside the provider's own infrastructure and controls, so nothing is disclosed to a third party. Using an unjoined computer, removing only server names or limiting use to cleared staff still sends patient data to an outside party with no agreement in place.

prompt: A team is putting AI-generated configuration changes into its change management process. Which practice best supports ethical and transparent use of AI?

options.text: Note the AI assistance in the change request and require human review and approval
Use AI only for changes made outside business hours so that fewer people are affected
Let the AI tool approve its own changes, because it can check its output faster than staff
Leave out any mention of AI so reviewers judge the change only on its technical merit

explanation: Being open about AI involvement and keeping a person accountable for approval are core ethical practices. Hiding AI use takes away information reviewers need to judge risk. Letting a tool approve its own output removes human oversight, and doing changes after hours does not address transparency or accountability.

prompt: A finance department must keep invoice records for seven years to meet a legal requirement, then make sure they are destroyed. Which data life cycle element addresses how long the records are kept?

options.text: Retention
Encryption
Identification
Classification

explanation: Retention sets how long data must be kept before disposal, which is exactly the seven-year rule. Classification assigns a sensitivity level, identification finds where the data is and what it is, and encryption protects the data but does not decide how long it is kept.

prompt: A company has found every share that holds employee records. It now needs to label each data set Public, Internal or Confidential so the right controls can be applied. Which data life cycle phase is this?

options.text: Identification
Classification
Retention
Disposal

explanation: Classification assigns sensitivity labels that decide which controls apply. Identification, finding the data, has already been done. Retention sets how long data is kept, and disposal is the secure destruction of data at the end of its life.

prompt: A batch of SSDs from decommissioned database servers held regulated customer data and must leave the company for recycling. Which method best ensures the data cannot be recovered?

options.text: Run a cryptographic or vendor secure erase, or shred the drives, and keep destruction records
Delete the partitions and run a quick format with a new filesystem on each drive
Overwrite free space once with zeros from the operating system before removing the drives from the servers
Degauss each SSD with a degausser rated for high-coercivity hard drive platters

explanation: SSDs should be sanitized with a cryptographic or firmware secure erase or destroyed, and documentation proves disposal took place. Degaussing does not work on flash memory, which does not store data magnetically. Deleting partitions or formatting leaves the data in place, and an OS overwrite cannot reach spare blocks the SSD controller has remapped.

prompt: A security team is worried that an attacker could record encrypted traffic today and decrypt it years from now with a quantum computer. The data must stay confidential for 15 years. What should the team plan?

options.text: Inventory where RSA and ECC key exchange are used and plan a move to NIST post-quantum algorithms like ML-KEM
Move from RSA to elliptic-curve key exchange, which quantum computers cannot efficiently break even with Shor's algorithm
Increase all RSA keys from 2048 to 4096 bits, which makes them resistant to attacks from quantum computers
Disable TLS 1.3 and require TLS 1.2, which supports a wider choice of cipher suites

explanation: This 'harvest now, decrypt later' threat is handled by post-quantum cryptography, and NIST standardized ML-KEM (FIPS 203) for key establishment. Shor's algorithm would break both RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography whatever the key size, so longer RSA keys or a move to ECC do not solve the problem. Going back from TLS 1.3 to TLS 1.2 adds no quantum resistance.

prompt: Several servers at an unstaffed branch office hold customer data, and the company worries that a stolen server's drives could be read on another machine. Which control addresses this risk most directly?

options.text: Full-disk encryption of the server volumes, with keys protected by a TPM
A host-based firewall that blocks all inbound ports except the ones in use
An access control list that limits the data folders to the branch staff group
TLS on all connections between the branch servers and the head office

explanation: Encryption of data at rest keeps a stolen drive unreadable without the key. TLS protects data in transit, not drives that are physically removed. ACLs and host firewalls are enforced by the running OS and do nothing once the drive is attached to another computer.

prompt: A packet capture shows that a legacy application sends customer records to its database server in clear text over the network. Which change protects this data in transit?

options.text: Turn on transparent data encryption for the database files on disk
Move the database files to a volume protected by full-disk encryption
Turn on TLS for the connection between the application and the database
Add an ACL on the database so only the application's service account can read it

explanation: TLS encrypts the traffic between the application and the database, protecting data in transit. Transparent data encryption and full-disk encryption protect data at rest on storage, not data crossing the network. An ACL controls who can access the database but does not stop someone from capturing the clear-text traffic.

prompt: After a new certificate from a public CA is installed on a web server, browsers accept the site but several Linux API clients fail with 'unable to get local issuer certificate.' The clients trust the public root CA. What is the most likely fix?

options.text: Replace the certificate with a self-signed one that the API clients are able to trust
Configure the server to send the intermediate CA certificate along with its own certificate
Install the web server's private key on each API client so it can validate the server
Disable certificate validation in the API clients until the CA sends a corrected certificate

explanation: Clients that trust only the root CA need the server to send the intermediate certificate to build the chain, and browsers often hide the gap by fetching or caching intermediates. A private key must never be given to clients and has no part in validation. A self-signed certificate or turning off validation weakens security instead of fixing the chain.

prompt: An internal web application uses a certificate issued by the company's enterprise CA. Domain-joined Windows clients trust it, but new non-domain Linux servers report that the certificate is untrusted. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Reissue the web server certificate with a longer validity period and a larger key
Change the application to use SSL 3.0 so the older protocol skips the trust check
Copy the web server certificate and its private key into each Linux server's store
Import the enterprise root CA certificate into the Linux servers' trusted store

explanation: Domain-joined Windows clients receive the enterprise root through the directory, but other systems must have the root CA certificate added to their trusted store. Validity period and key size do not change who issued the certificate. Spreading the private key is a serious security risk, and SSL 3.0 is insecure and still validates certificates.

prompt: A compliance scan reports that a web server still accepts SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0 connections. Which configuration should the administrator apply?

options.text: Disable TLS 1.0 only, because SSL 3.0 is still considered secure for web traffic
Disable SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1, and allow only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3
Keep all protocol versions enabled and replace the certificate with one using a larger key
Disable every TLS version and allow only SSL 3.0, which is the newer protocol

explanation: SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are deprecated and insecure, so only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 should be allowed. SSL 3.0 is not secure, and it is older than TLS, not newer. A larger certificate key does not fix weaknesses in the protocol versions themselves.

prompt: A data center uses badge readers on the server room door, a firewall between the server VLAN and user VLANs, and NTFS permissions that limit a share to the HR group. Which control type is the NTFS permission?

options.text: Network control
Deterrent control
Logical control
Physical control

explanation: An access control list such as NTFS permissions is a logical (technical) control enforced by the OS. The badge reader is a physical control and the firewall is a network control. A deterrent control discourages an attacker, such as a warning sign, rather than enforcing file permissions.

prompt: Management wants proof that an attacker could actually reach payroll data by chaining weaknesses on the server network. Authorized testers will work under agreed rules of engagement. Which kind of test is needed?

options.text: Penetration test
Tabletop exercise
Vulnerability scan
Configuration baseline review

explanation: A penetration test actively exploits and chains weaknesses to show real impact within agreed rules. A vulnerability scan lists likely weaknesses but does not exploit them to prove impact. A tabletop exercise is a discussion-based plan rehearsal, and a baseline review compares settings to a standard.

prompt: An online payments company has a recovery time objective of 15 minutes for its transaction platform. Which type of DR site meets this requirement?

options.text: Hot site
Cold site
Warm site
Off-site tape vault

explanation: A hot site runs ready equipment with near-current replicated data and can take over within minutes. A warm site has hardware but needs data restored and configuration, which usually takes hours to days. A cold site provides only space and power, and a tape vault stores media but no running systems.

prompt: A company's DR site is 8 km from its main data center, and both sit on the same coastal flood plain often hit by hurricanes. What is the main weakness of this design?

options.text: The distance forces the use of asynchronous replication, which is never acceptable
The DR site must be inside the same building to be classed as a valid hot site
The sites are too far apart for any kind of synchronous or asynchronous data replication to work
A single regional disaster could hit both sites, so the DR site belongs in another region

explanation: Geographic separation is meant to keep one event, such as a hurricane or flood, from hitting both sites. Eight kilometers is close enough for even synchronous replication, so distance is not the problem. A DR site in the same building defeats the purpose, and asynchronous replication is widely used when its RPO is acceptable.

prompt: The DR team wants to walk through its ransomware recovery plan with IT, legal and communications staff in a meeting room, discussing each person's actions without touching any systems. Which test type is this?

options.text: Parallel production test
Live failover
Simulated failover
Tabletop exercise

explanation: A tabletop exercise is a discussion-based run-through of the plan with no impact on systems. A live failover actually moves production to the DR site. A simulated failover brings up replicated systems in an isolated environment, and a parallel test runs recovery systems alongside production, both of which use real systems.

prompt: A company has adopted a security configuration baseline for its 150 RHEL servers. Every month the team must check each server's settings against the baseline profile and produce a machine-readable compliance report showing which rules pass or fail. Which tool fits this task?

options.text: A penetration test, in which testers try to exploit each server monthly
OpenSCAP, evaluating the servers against an SCAP baseline profile
Nmap, scanning each server's open ports and running service versions
A tabletop exercise, in which staff review the baseline document together

explanation: OpenSCAP evaluates systems against SCAP content, such as CIS or DISA STIG profiles from the SCAP Security Guide, and reports pass or fail for each configuration rule. Nmap discovers ports and services but does not check configuration settings against a baseline. A penetration test looks for exploitable weaknesses and is too costly to repeat monthly as a compliance check. A tabletop exercise discusses a plan and does not inspect any server.

prompt: A retail database is backed up every night at 11:00 PM. The business now says it can lose no more than one hour of transactions after a failure. Which objective does the current backup design fail to meet?

options.text: Mean time to recover (MTTR)
Recovery point objective (RPO)
Recovery time objective (RTO)
Mean time between failures (MTBF)

explanation: RPO is the largest acceptable amount of data loss measured in time, and nightly backups can lose up to 24 hours of data. RTO is how quickly service must be restored, not how much data is lost. MTBF describes how often a component fails, and MTTR is the average time taken to restore service.

prompt: A hosting contract promises 99.9% availability per 30-day month. About how much total downtime does that allow each month?

options.text: 432 minutes
7.2 hours
4.32 minutes
43.2 minutes

explanation: A 30-day month has 43,200 minutes, and 0.1% of that is 43.2 minutes. 4.32 minutes matches 99.99% availability. 7.2 hours (432 minutes) matches 99% availability, which allows ten times more downtime than 99.9%.

prompt: Before setting RTO and RPO values, a company needs to find out which business processes are critical, how they depend on IT systems, and what each hour of downtime would cost. Which activity provides this?

options.text: Business impact analysis (BIA)
Service-level agreement (SLA)
Vulnerability scan
Tabletop exercise

explanation: A BIA identifies critical processes, their dependencies and the impact of disruption, which is the basis for RTO and RPO. A vulnerability scan looks for technical weaknesses. An SLA is a service commitment that may use those targets, and a tabletop exercise tests a plan that already exists.

prompt: A defense contractor must harden its Red Hat Enterprise Linux servers to the configuration guides published by the U.S. Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA). Which guidance should the team apply?

options.text: NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) functions
Center for Internet Security (CIS) Benchmarks
Security Technical Implementation Guides
ISO/IEC 27001 information security controls

explanation: DISA publishes STIGs, which are detailed hardening guides used for U.S. Department of Defense systems. ISO/IEC 27001 defines requirements for an information security management system, not host settings. CIS Benchmarks are hardening guides from the Center for Internet Security, not DISA, and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework is a high-level risk framework.

prompt: Operators need a short, step-by-step document for one task: failing over the payroll database cluster and checking that the application reconnects. Which document type fits best?

options.text: Runbook
Service-level agreement
Business continuity policy
Network diagram

explanation: A runbook gives detailed, ordered steps for a specific operational task such as a cluster failover. A BC policy sets high-level direction and responsibilities rather than task steps. A network diagram shows connectivity, and an SLA defines service commitments to customers.

prompt: An auditor asks how the company would find out who added a user account to the Domain Admins group last month. What must be in place to answer this?

options.text: A rule that every administrator uses a password of at least 20 characters
Auditing of group membership changes, with events kept in a central log store
A weekly vulnerability scan of every domain controller in the forest
A monthly export of the Domain Admins member list saved to a protected file share for later review

explanation: Auditing group membership changes records who made each change and when, and central retention keeps the evidence available. A monthly member list shows who is in the group but not who added them. Vulnerability scans and password length rules do not record membership changes.

prompt: A company bought perpetual licenses for its backup software five years ago and let the annual maintenance contract lapse two years ago. What is the most likely effect?

options.text: The software stops working at the next license check, because perpetual licenses need maintenance
It must buy new perpetual licenses before it can install security patches already released
It keeps getting updates and support, because those come with every perpetual license
It can keep using the version it owns but gets no updates, new versions or vendor support

explanation: A perpetual license grants ongoing use of the purchased version, while maintenance covers updates, upgrades and support. Losing maintenance does not normally disable perpetual software. Whether an existing license can be renewed depends on the vendor, but updates and support come with maintenance, not with the perpetual license itself.

prompt: After assessing the risk of a costly data breach, a company buys a cyber insurance policy to cover breach response and legal costs. Which risk response is this?

options.text: Acceptance
Mitigation
Avoidance
Transference

explanation: Insurance moves the financial impact of a risk to another party, which is transference. Avoidance removes the risky activity completely, acceptance means taking no action and absorbing the impact, and mitigation lowers likelihood or impact with controls.

prompt: Developers want a copy of the production customer database in the test environment to reproduce a bug. The database holds names, addresses and national ID numbers. What is the best data handling approach?

options.text: Load an exact copy and delete it once the bug is fixed and the change is deployed
Load an exact copy onto an encrypted test server so the data stays protected at rest
Mask or anonymize the PII before loading the copy into the test environment
Load an exact copy but limit access to the test environment to the developers who are working on the bug

explanation: Masking or anonymizing PII removes the privacy exposure while keeping realistic data for testing. Limiting access, deleting the data later or encrypting the test server all still put real PII in a less controlled non-production environment for some time.

prompt: An administrator changed a core switch ACL on a Friday afternoon without telling anyone, and the backup network went offline all weekend. Which process would most directly have prevented this?

options.text: A data retention policy that defines how long switch configuration backups are kept
Change management requiring a documented request, impact review and approval
A business impact analysis that ranks the backup system as a critical service
Asset management that records the purchase date and warranty for every switch

explanation: Change management requires changes to be documented, reviewed for impact and approved, which would have caught or scheduled the ACL change. Asset records track hardware details, a BIA ranks services but does not control changes, and a retention policy decides how long data is kept.

prompt: During a ransomware incident, the attackers used a stolen backup administrator account to delete every restore point on the backup repository before encrypting production. Which change best prevents this next time?

options.text: Turn on compression and deduplication on the repository so more restore points fit on the disks
Take incremental backups every hour instead of nightly so more recent restore points are created
Change the backup administrator password every 30 days and require it to be at least 16 characters
Write backups to immutable storage, such as object storage with a compliance-mode retention lock

explanation: Immutable backups, such as WORM storage or object lock in compliance mode, cannot be changed or deleted before retention ends, even by an administrator account. Password rotation helps but does not stop an attacker who already holds the credentials. Compression, deduplication and more frequent backups add restore points that the same account can still delete.

prompt: A company wants at least one copy of its backups that ransomware cannot reach over any network, even if the whole domain is compromised. Which strategy meets this goal?

options.text: Keep backups on a separate volume of the backup server that is hidden from users
Copy backups to a cloud bucket mapped as a drive letter on the backup server
Replicate backups to a second NAS in the same data center that is joined to the same domain
Write weekly backups to tape, eject the cartridges and store them off-site

explanation: An air-gapped copy is physically or logically disconnected, and ejected tapes stored off-site have no network path for an attacker to use. A domain-joined NAS, a mapped cloud drive and a hidden volume are all reachable from compromised systems over the network.

prompt: A file server gets a full backup every Sunday night and a differential backup every other night. The server fails on Thursday morning. Which backups are needed to restore it to the latest possible point?

options.text: Sunday's full backup and the Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday differential backups
Sunday's full backup and Wednesday night's differential backup
Sunday's full backup by itself, because differential backups only hold the changed metadata
Wednesday night's differential backup by itself, because it holds the whole server

explanation: A differential backup holds every change since the last full backup, so the full backup plus the latest differential restores the server. Earlier differentials are already included in Wednesday's. A differential cannot be restored without its full backup, and it holds changed data, not only metadata.

prompt: A server gets a full backup on Sunday night and incremental backups Monday through Wednesday nights. It fails on Thursday morning. Which backups must be restored?

options.text: The Wednesday incremental backup only, because each incremental holds all of the changes
Sunday's full backup and the Wednesday incremental backup only, because it is the newest
The Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday incrementals only, because the full backup is already on disk
Sunday's full backup, then the Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday incremental backups in that order

explanation: Each incremental holds only the changes since the previous backup, so the full backup and every later incremental must be applied in order. Wednesday's incremental alone is missing the Monday and Tuesday changes. The failed server's disk cannot be counted on, so the full backup must be restored first.

prompt: Weekly full backups of a large file server overrun the backup window and load the production storage. The backup software can build a new full backup on the backup server by combining the last full backup with later incrementals. What is this called?

options.text: Image-level backup
Block-level snapshot
Differential backup
Synthetic full backup

explanation: A synthetic full is built on the backup target from an earlier full backup and later incrementals, so production does not have to be read again. A differential copies all changes since the last full from the source. An image-level backup captures a whole system from the source, and a snapshot is a point-in-time copy on the primary storage.

prompt: A small company keeps its production data on a file server and nightly backups on a NAS in the same rack. What is the minimum change that brings it into line with the 3-2-1 backup rule?

options.text: Add a third copy on different media, such as cloud or tape, kept off-site
Add a second NAS in the same rack and mirror the first NAS onto it every night
Configure RAID 6 on the NAS so the backups survive two disk failures in the array
Take hourly snapshots of the file server volume and keep them for 30 days

explanation: The 3-2-1 rule calls for three copies of data on two different types of media, with one copy off-site, and an off-site cloud or tape copy adds the missing copy, media type and location. A second NAS in the same rack is not off-site, RAID protects against disk failure rather than keeping a separate copy, and snapshots usually stay on the same storage.

prompt: For two years the backup console has shown every nightly job as successful, but no one has ever restored any data from it. What should the administrator start doing?

options.text: Run test restores at a regular interval and verify the restored data and applications
Swap the backup media for faster disks so that the jobs finish sooner
Double the retention period so that more restore points are available if one is damaged
